items.note: Village houses are generally of mud with a ground floor only; in towns the better-off live in pakka houses of brick or stone.
Prevalent dress of the agricultural class: short dhoti, bandi and pagri for males, lehenga, odhni and choli for females.
Lists among important fairs a 7 days' Shivaratri fair in February/March at Udaipur (Vidisha district).
Wheat is the staple food of the district; poorer classes eat bajra, jowar or gram bread.
Tradition links the region to Raja Bhoj's time, with the classical dancer 'Lavanya Sundari'; ral is a characteristic folk-dance performed by professionals known as bednis.
Agriculture's importance: 75 per cent of workers in 1961 were cultivators or agricultural labourers.
Comparative richness of the Vidisha cultivator attributed to rich soil; the tract was sparsely cultivated not long ago, with Luard in 1907 noting the finest soil lying fallow.
